prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the 3D layout as the camera wearer turns right across the five frames from the kitchen counter and sink area (roughly 2.5 to 3.0 m away on the left in frames 1–3) past an open doorway (3.5 to 5.0 m deep in the center) toward a foreground wooden island (0.4 m at the bottom edge to 1.8 m at the far end in frames 4–5). In frames 4 and 5, it clearly separates the near island surface and objects within the camera wearer's arm's reach—a foil-lined tray at the bottom edge (0.4–0.6 m), a seasoning bottle on the right (0.6 m), and a dark water bottle in the center (0.8 m) that partially occludes a white cup behind it (1.1 m)—from a seated person on the far right side of the island (1.3–1.6 m away) and cabinets behind them (1.8–2.2 m). The seated person's silhouette shows their torso and head angled forward and slightly left over the counter toward a bowl within their own arm's reach (0.2–0.4 m in front of them) rather than facing the camera wearer. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the continuous distance gradient across the island and the depth discontinuity through the doorway in dark or motion-blurred frames (especially frame 3) much easier to read. However, it is unreliable in frame 1 where heavy motion blur flattens the counter and doorway into an indistinct dark region, and across frames 4–5 where thin or low-relief items on the island (the knife, cell phone, and stacked white platters) merge nearly seamlessly into the tabletop plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies discrete objects across the scene as the camera wearer pans right, detecting the left-wall sink (2.5 m), oven (2.8 m), microwave above the oven (2.8 m), and a distant bowl on the island (1.6 m) in frame 2, before picking up the close island arrangement and the seated person (1.3–1.6 m away on the right) in frames 4 and 5. In frames 4 and 5, it localizes the person seated behind the right edge of the island facing toward the tabletop, with a small bowl (1.2 m) and cell phone (1.2 m) directly in front of their arms, a central bottle (0.8 m) and knife (0.6 m) within the camera wearer's reach, a second bottle at the lower right (0.6 m in frame 4), and a fruit bowl at the far upper-left corner of the island (1.6 m, about 0.8 m from the person). The masks highlight small or low-contrast items like the dark cell phone and small bowl next to the person's hands that are harder to isolate at a glance in the RGB frames, while showing the central bottle occluding the lower edge of the person's bowl in frame 4. However, the map is completely blank during the motion-blurred pans in frames 1 and 3, misses the person entirely when they are partially cut off at the right edge of frame 2, and mislabels the near foil-lined baking tray (0.5 m) and the stacked white rectangular platters (0.9 m) as 'sink' in frames 4 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely empty across the five-frame turn, failing to detect any valid human keypoints in frames 1, 3, and 4 despite the seated person being partially visible at the right edge of frames 2 and 3 (around 1.5 m away) and clearly visible on the right side of the island in frames 4 and 5 (1.3–1.6 m away). In frame 5, a partial yellow upper-body skeleton appears on the seated person's right shoulder, elbow, and wrist (around 1.3–1.4 m from the camera wearer), showing their right arm resting on the counter and reaching forward toward the small bowl within 0.3 m of their body while they face angled left and downward away from the camera wearer. No magenta hand skeletons are detected in any frame, even though both of the person's hands are visible on the tabletop in frames 4 and 5 and the lower body remains occluded beneath the island surface. This map is highly unreliable here: aside from missing the person in frames 2–4, it hallucinates a false horizontal yellow skeleton along the kitchen sink and countertop (2.5–2.8 m away on the left) in frame 2 where no person exists.
